" Know that the disk of the sun is in the fist of the angel, but the heart of the lovers is in the fist of the King-majestic and high is He!

14.text:
Say, O Prophet: the command to speak opens the verse, and what follows is a question put in the first person so that the Prophet is the one asking it in front of them. Will I take any guardian other than Allah: the question is a refusal dressed as a question, and the word guardian covers the one to whom a person turns for protection and help, so the verse is not asking about a point of detail but about where the whole life is directed. the Originator of the heavens and the earth: the One being described is the One who brought the heavens and the earth into being without any earlier model, and the description is placed in the middle of the question where it does the most work, since it names the maker of everything a guardian would have to compete with. Who provides for all and is not in need of provision, Say: the provision is the second mark of the One being described, and the contrast is exact, since the creatures are fed and the Creator is not, and the verse begins a second sentence with the same command, so the answer is put twice in the mouth of the one who asks. I have been commanded to be the first to submit and not be one of the polytheists: the obedience is stated as a command laid on him rather than as an achievement, and the order of the two halves matters, since the submission comes first and the warning about the partners comes after it. The word first is one of the things the sources stop at, since it means first in his own community and among the people he speaks to. The verse is addressed to people who had asked for proof and were given a question about the master of everything, and it puts the Prophet's own position in front of them, that he has no guardian but Allah and that he is the first of those who submit. The verse after takes the same obedience one step further, and the fear named there is part of the same answer.

**The guardian they were invited to take.**

Does it make sense that I take any one other than Allah as a guardian and a protector from whom I seek help? Say to them ‘Shall I take as a protector to worship other than God the Originator of the heavens and the earth the One Who has created them without any precedent He Who feeds Who gives sustenance and is not fed?’ and is not given sustenance.

**The Creator of the heavens and the earth.**

The meaning here is, I will not take a guardian except Allah, without partners, for He is the Creator of the heavens and earth Who orignated them without precedent,. Allah is the One Who created the heavens and the earth without any precedent. (Shall I choose for a protecting friend) for a lord to worship (other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feedeth) provides sustenance to the servants (and is never fed?) is never provided sustenance; it is also said:

**The One who feeds, and is never fed.**

(And it is He Who feeds but is not fed.) For He sustains His creatures without needing them. "And it is He Who feeds but He does not eat." meaning, Allah does not eat. To Him belongs the attribute of generosity, so He feeds. (All praise is due to Allah, Who feeds but is never fed, He bestowed bounty unto us, Who gave us guidance and fed us, gave us something to drink, covered our nakedness; and for every favor He has given us. All praise is due to Allah, praise that should not be neglected, my Lord, all the while affirming that we will never be able to duly thank Him; nor be appreciative enough of Him, nor be free of needing Him. All thanks and praises are due to Allah Who fed us the food, gave us the drink, covered our nudity, guided us from misguidance, gave us sight from blindness, and honored us above many of His creaturers. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of all that exists.") He is the One Who gives provision to whichever of His servants He wishes, and none of His servants provide for Him. He is not in any need of His servants, but His servants are in need of Him. He is not helped in providing sustenance to His servants. He does not partake of daily provision, but He assigns daily provision to the servants.

**The command to be the first to submit.**

Say ‘I have been commanded to be the first to submit to God from among this community and it was said to me “Do not be among those who associate others” ’ with Him. (Say: "Verily, I am commanded to be the first of those who submit themselves to Allah as (Muslims).") from this Ummah,. (I am ordered to be the first to surrender (unto Him) the first to embrace Islam; it is also said that this means: the first among the people of his time to worship sincerely and declare Allah's divine Oneness. My Lord has instructed me to be the first one from this nation to submit and be humble. Allah then said to His servant and Messenger Muhammad , whom He sent with the pure Tawhid and the straight religion, commanding him to call the people to Allah's straight path;.

**The heart that has no room for another.**

After the brightness of His solicitude has fallen upon me, shall I gaze on someone else in the two houses?"5 "The sun of solicitude and kind favor has shone upon me from the Majestic and Exalted Threshold and taken care of my business without me in the two worlds, lighting up my heart with the eternal love and adorning it with the ornament of intimacy. Some times the grasp of the attributes explains the polish of my heart's mirror by virtue of solicitude: With all this good fortune, rank, solicitude, and kind favor, how would it be appropriate for my heart to request someone else or to gaze upon this world and the afterworld? " Hence he said concerning this world, "What do I have to do with this world? Man is a creature with a will of his own and that is why voluntary worship is required of him. Those who do not choose to exercise their will rightly, do not deserve a share in God’s bounties, not having fulfilled the purpose of their creation. But the things on which his arrogance depends for support have no value in this universe. So, on the Day of Judgement, only those who had sought out the real support, who had made the true faith the religion of their lives, will be successful. Say, O Messenger, to the idolaters who worship idols and other things together with Allah: (And be not thou (O Muhammad) of the idolaters) with the idolaters, following their religion. (And be not you of the idolaters. Say: "I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the torment of a Mighty Day.")[6:14-15], the Day of Resurrection,. He gave me such eminence at the forefront of acceptance that sometimes He puts up with my disdain: Sometimes the assessor of the beginningless and endless register turns over the acceptance and rejection of the creatures to my threshold: (And I created not the Jinn and humans except that they should worship Me (Alone).)[51:56] Some scholars read it,. On that Day those who admitted the reality and surrendered themselves to God will come to the fore and those who did not, having led a life of arrogance and obstinacy in the world, will be the losers.

15.text:
Say, I truly fear if I were to disobey my Lord the torment of a tremendous Day. The verse gives the Prophet words about himself, and the words are a warning to the people who were listening. Say, I truly fear is a sentence about the Prophet's own state, and the fear is stated plainly so that no one can think the commands were given to someone who could not fail them. if I were to disobey my Lord: the condition is put in the open, and the sources notice that the noble messenger is protected from sin, so the sentence cannot be about something that might happen to him; it is a way of showing how heavy the command is, since the one who carries it speaks about it as if he could slip. the torment of a tremendous Day: the end of the disobedience is named as a day rather than as a penalty, and the day is called tremendous so that the reader feels the scale before he hears any detail. The verse sits directly after the command to submit and the warning against partners, and it gives the reason the command matters, so the reader is taken from the order to the consequence in one step. The wording closes on the day and leaves the punishment unnamed, which is how this passage has handled the last things from the beginning, and the verses that follow turn to the mercy shown to the one who is spared it.

**The fear the Prophet is told to speak of.**

Say ‘Indeed I fear if I should rebel against my Lord by worshipping other than Him the chastisement of a dreadful day’ namely the Day of Resurrection. If I go against Allah by committing that which He has prohibited (such as associating partners with Him) or by leaving out what He has instructed me to do (such as having faith and doing good actions), then I fear that He will punish me with a severe punishment on the Day of Rising. (I fear) I know, (if I rebel against my Lord) and worship other than Him, I would be reverting back to your religion, (the retribution of an Awful Day) I would face then a tremendous torment on an Awful Day; it is also said that this means: In the previous verses, the command given was to shun Shirk and believe in the perfect power of Allah Jalla Sha'nuhu mentioned there-in.

**The Prophet protected, and the warning for the community.**

In the first of the present verses , the punishment for the contravention of this command has been mentioned in a particularly endearing manner, that is, the Holy Prophet has been commanded' that he should tell the people that should he too (God forbid) come to contravene the command of His Lord, then, he too has the fear of the punishment of the day of Qiyamah. It is obvious that the noble Messenger of Allah is (Divinely) protected from every sin - so, the likelihood of disobedience coming from him simply does not exist. But, by mentioning this hypothetical situation, the purpose is to convey the message to the community that the contravention of the Divine command is so serious a matter that even the greatest prophet cannot stand excused from it - if not him, who else?

**The Day of Resurrection, and no doubt in it.**

(Indeed He will gather you together on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.) swearing by His Most Honored Self that He will gather His servants,. (For appointed meeting of a known Day.)[56:50], the Day of Resurrection that will certainly occur, and there is no doubt for His believing servants in this fact. (Those who destroy themselves) on the Day of Resurrection,. On that Day those who admitted the reality and surrendered themselves to God will come to the fore and those who did not, having led a life of arrogance and obstinacy in the world, will be the losers. So, on the Day of Judgement, only those who had sought out the real support, who had made the true faith the religion of their lives, will be successful. On that Day God will take into His hands the direct control of the rest of the world. On that Day God’s scale of justice will be operative.

16.text:
Whoever is spared the torment of that Day will have certainly been shown Allah's mercy. The verse names the person who escapes rather than the punishment, and the shape of the sentence tells the reader where the emphasis lies. Whoever is spared the torment of that Day: the wording is passive, and the sources notice it, since the person spared did not save himself and the sparing is done to him. of that Day links the sentence to the day named in the verse before, so the reader is still standing at the same scene. Then the second half explains what the escape means: will have certainly been shown Allah's mercy. The mercy is named as the cause of the escape, so the reader learns that the outcome is not a reward earned by a person's own strength but a favour given. And that is the absolute triumph: the verse ends with a word that carries the sense of winning decisively, and the sources keep the whole meaning of it as salvation, since the one who is kept from the fire and brought into the garden cannot lose. The order is worth following, since the verse goes from the sparing to the mercy to the triumph, and the last two are the explanation of the first. The mercy is not described as something the person has earned, and the sources keep it that way, since the one who is spared is shown mercy rather than paid what he deserved. The verses before had set out the fear of the tremendous Day and the command that came with it, and this verse gives the reader the other side of the same day, so that the passage keeps warning and hope together. The verses that follow turn to the harm and the blessing that touch a person in this life, so the reader is carried from the last day back to his own day.

**The day, and the mercy that averts the retribution.**

(He from whom) such retribution (is averted on that day) the Day of Judgement ((Allah) hath in truth had mercy on him) He had preserved and forgiven him. (And be not you of the idolaters. Say: "I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the torment of a Mighty Day.")[6:14-15], the Day of Resurrection,. Allah states that He is the King and Owner of the heavens and earth and all of what is in them, and that He has written mercy on His Most Honorable Self. It means that the punishment of the day of Resurrection (al-Mahshar) is extremely horrendous and harsh. Who is averted from (such a torment) on that Day; then He (Allah) has surely been Merciful to him. This tells us that deliverance from punishment and admittance into the Paradise are inseparable from each other.

**The mercy of the One who spares.**

After that, it was said: ‌ ‌ (Whoever is spared from it that day is, indeed, blessed with His mercy). Whoever finds this removed from him or her should know that it was great mercy from Allah. (When Allah created the creation, He wrote in a Book that He has with Him above the Throne; 'My mercy overcomes My anger.') Allah said;. The person from whom Allah keeps away and removes the punishment on the Day of Rising has attained success through the mercy of Allah.

**The triumph, and what it means.**

He from whom it is averted read passive yusraf ‘it is averted’ namely ‘the chastisement’; or read active yasrif ‘He averts’ namely ‘God’ as the subject; the referential noun has been omitted on that day He the Exalted One will have had mercy on him He will have desired good for him; that is the manifest triumph evident salvation. (That) forgiveness (will be the signal triumph) a great salvation. Such salvation and safety from the punishment is a clear victory which no other victory can equal.

17.text:
If Allah touches you with harm, none can undo it except Him. The verse puts the smallest unit of human experience in front of the reader and follows it to its end. If Allah touches you with harm: the touch is the word for something that reaches a person directly, and the harm is left unnamed so that the sentence covers illness and poverty and every other shape it takes. none can undo it except Him: the second phrase closes every other door at once, and the wording does not say that the others are not strong enough but that they cannot do it at all. And if He touches you with a blessing: the verse then names the other side, and the blessing is also left unnamed so that it covers health and wealth and everything a person is given, and the reader is shown that the two come from the same hand. He is Most Capable of everything: the last phrase gives the reason, since the One who can give a gift can also take it back, and the power named here is not left to be guessed at. The verse is addressed to the Prophet and through him to every reader, and its two halves stand in the same order as the days of a life, since harm and good come one after the other and both are in the same hand. The verses that come before had ended with a mention of mercy and the day of gathering, and this verse brings the same subject down to what happens in a person's own body and home, where the same two hands are at work in a smaller frame and the reader can see them without any argument. The verses that follow raise the same argument to the mastery of the Lord over His servants, so the reader is carried from the small scale to the large one.

**The harm, and the One who removes it.**

And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He, and if He touches you with good, then He is able to do all things And He is the Irresistible, above His servants, and He is the All-Wise, Well-Acquainted with all things Say: If any calamity from Allah afflicts you, O son of Adam, there is no one who can remove it from you besides Allah. (And if Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but He, and if He touches you with good, then He is able to do all things.) Similarly, Allah said,. And if God touches you with an affliction a trial such as an illness or impoverishment then none can remove it none can lift it except Him; and if He touches you with good such as health and affluence then He has power over all things including His touching you with this and none other than Him has the power to remove it from you.

**The harm and the blessing, from the same hand.**

(If Allah touch thee with) if Allah brings on you (affliction) hardship and penury, (there is none that can relieve therefrom) none can lift them from you (save Him, and if He touch thee with) if Allah brings on you (good fortune) blessing and wealth ((there is none that can impair it); for He is Able to do all things): hardship and penury, blessing and wealth. Allah states that He Alone brings benefit or harm, and that He does what He wills with His creatures, none can resist His judgment or prevent what He decrees,. Just as in creating harm, He is one and unique, so also in repelling harm, He is unique and without equal.

**The help that is asked of Him alone.**

To-day, there is a very large number of Muslims who would, rather than call upon Allah and pray to Him in their hour of distress, cry for help in all sorts of names, but do not seem to remember the name of Allah. And understand it very clearly that the help of Allah is with patience, and comfort with hardship, and prosperity with adversity.' (This Hadkh also appears in Tirmidhi and the Musnad of Ahmad with sound chains of authority) This being so, no human being is capable of causing any event to occur, because no human being is in control of the universe. (O Allah, there is none Who can avert what You grant or give what You deprive, and no fortune ever helps the fortunate against You.) This is why Allah said,.

18.text:
He reigns supreme over His creation. The verse follows the harm and the blessing of the one before it with the mastery that stands behind both, and the order is the lesson. He reigns supreme over His creation: the word for reigning is the word for being above and beyond reach, and the creation is named as the thing that lies below it, so the sentence is a statement about power rather than about place. And He is the All-Wise, All-Aware: the two names complete the sentence and guard it, since power without wisdom would be a blind force and wisdom without knowledge would miss what it judges. The Aware is named last because it reaches the inside of a person, and the reader who has just heard about harm and blessing is told that nothing he hides is outside the account. The two halves of the verse answer each other, since the first states that nothing can resist the Lord and the second states that nothing is done without reason or without being seen. The verse also closes a run that began with the ownership of the heavens and the earth and went through the mercy and the gathering, so it gathers the argument into two names at the end. The verses that follow turn to the witness that is called for next, so the reader is being prepared for an argument about evidence after a statement about power.

**The dominant power over His slaves.**

At the end of verse 18, it was said: ‌ ‌ 18 (And He is dominant over His slaves, and He is the Ali-Wise, the All-Aware). He is the One Who is powerful and dominant and nothing can overpower or defeat Him: everything is subservient to Him. It means that the mastery of Allah Ta ala prevails over His servants in the absolute sense and that everyone remains under His power and control all the time.

**The Wise, the All-Aware.**

He is the Vanquisher the Omnipotent for Whom nothing is impossible Superior is He over His servants and He is the Wise in His creation the Aware of their innermost thoughts as well as their outward actions. (He is the Omnipotent) the All-Conquering (over His slaves, and He is the Wise) in His command and decree, (the Knower) of His created beings and their works. The different parts of the vast universe spread out before us are so interconnected that for an event to occur, the coordination of the whole universe is necessary. Since he who is in remembrance is happy with You, why is he who is happy with You lamenting?

**The power and the knowledge together.**

Thus, by the word, al-Qahir (the Dominant) pointed to is the perfect power of Allah Ta ala and, by the word, al-Hakim (the All-Wise), His all-encompassing knowledge - and the two tell us that perfection in knowledge and power are the sole attributes of Almighty Allah and it is only Him that they belong to. This is the reason why no human being, no matter how great, whether a prophet close to Allah, or the most powerful ruler of the world, nine of them come out successful in everything they do, nor is every wish of theirs granted. (O Allah, there is none Who can avert what You grant or give what You deprive, and no fortune ever helps the fortunate against You.) This is why Allah said,. This is because they received good news from the previous Messengers and Prophets about the coming of Muhammad , his attributes, homeland, his migration, and the description of his Ummah.

19.text:
Ask them, O Prophet: the verse opens with a question put to the people who had been demanding a witness, and the asking is itself part of the answer. Who is the best witness, Say, Allah is: the question asks after the greatest of those who can bear witness, and the word best is what makes the question a ladder, since the reader is being taken up from the witnesses he would think of first, and the answer is given at once, since the sources notice that the Prophet was told to answer rather than wait for them and that the answer was going to close the matter. He is a Witness between me and you: the witness is named as the one who stands between the two sides, and the wording places the Prophet and his people in the same frame, with Allah as the one who sees both. And this Quran has been revealed to me so that, with it: the Quran is then named as the thing the Prophet has been given, and the giving is stated plainly so that the witness is not left without a sign to point to. I may warn you and whoever it reaches: the warning is for the people in front of him and then for every person the book reaches, and the sources notice how far the second half carries the mission. Do you pagans testify that there are other gods besides Allah, Then say, I will never testify to this, And say, There is only One God: the question is put back to them, and it names what they had been saying in their own words, and the answer that follows is a refusal placed in the Prophet's mouth as a thing he will not do even to please them, and the verse then states the content of his own testimony. And I totally reject whatever idols you associate with Him: the last phrase severs him from the partners they worship, so the verse ends where the sūrah began, on the difference between the Creator and the equals set up beside Him. The verses that follow turn to those who were given the Scripture before, so the argument is carried from the idolaters to the people who had a book.

**The greatest witness.**

When they said to the Prophet s ‘Bring us someone to testify to the truth of your prophethood for the People of the Scripture have denied you’ the following was revealed Say to them ‘What thing is greatest in testimony?’ shahādatan this is for specification and is derived from the implied subject of the sentence. (Say: "What thing is the most great in witness") or what is the greatest witness,. Which thing is greatest and most honoured as a witness to my truthfulness? Allah is the greatest and most honoured witness to my truthfulness. You tell them whose witness could be greater than that of Allah, within whose power lies the gain and loss of everyone in the world?

**The witness between me and you.**

Say ‘God — even if they do not say this there is no other response — He is Witness between me and you to my truthfulness; and this Qur’ān has been revealed to me that I may warn you that I may make you fear O people of Makkah thereby and whomever it may reach wa-man balagha this is a supplement to the suffixed pronoun ‘you’ of undhira-kum ‘I may warn you’ that is to say whomever among men and jinn the Qur’ān may reach. Then, you tell them that Allah is the witness between me and you The witness of Allah refers to those miracles and signs which Allah Ta ala made manifest to confirm the veracity of the prophethood of the Holy Prophet . (Say: "Allah (the Most Great!) is Witness between you and I") for He knows what I brought you and what you will answer me with,. When they said to the Prophet ﷺ bring us a witness to testify that you are a prophet, Allah said: " There is no bearing witness more truthful than the Real's own bearing witness to what He wit nessed at the first.

**The Quran, and whom it reaches.**

This proves that the Holy Prophet is the Last Prophet and the Qur’ an will keep reaching until the day of Qiyamah. (And this Qur'an hath been inspired in me) and that Gabriel has brought down this Qur'an to me, (that I may warn therewith you) with the Qur'an (and whomsoever it may reach) I am a warner to him. The Quran has been revealed so that, before the arrival of the time of Judgement, people may be made aware of what awaits them. So God, the only Being who is capable of settling this dispute, has given an arbiter to the people in the form of the Quran. Those who are assigned the task of delivering this message to the people will be free of the responsibility once they have fully conveyed the message; but those to whom it is delivered will be free in the eyes of God only when they have accepted it and reformed themselves accordingly. May Allah keep that person hale and hearty who heard a saying of mine, committed it to his memory and then conveyed it to my Ummah. This is important because it generally happens that a person may not himself appreciate the sense of what is said but which would be understood much better by a person of later times to whom the first person has conveyed it.

**Do you bear witness that there are gods beside Allah.**

(Do ye) O people of Makkah (in sooth bear witness that there are gods beside Allah) i.e. idols: you say that they are Allah's daughters? And if they bear witness, (Say: I bear no such witness) with you. Do you, even after the witness of Allah Ta ala Himself, stand to witness against Him by saying that there are other gods too along with Allah? You, O idolaters, believe that there are others worthy of worship together with Allah. I do not bear witness to what you have acknowledged as it is false. In the on-going struggle between the proponents, on the one hand of Truth and on the other of falsehood, the only decisive factor is the Book of God. One who is not in agreement with the decision of the Quran runs the risk of being forced to accept its verdict in the Hereafter after much degradation and punishment.

**The bearing witness of the creatures.**

On the first day, at the beginningless covenant, with true words and pure speech, He reported of the unitary existence, the self-sufficient being, the endless majesty, the eternal beauty, the con tinuous Essence, and the self-standing attributes. With His own gentleness He is teaching the servants to bear witness in their measure to His oneness and solitariness, just as He bears witness as is fitting for Him. Oth ers, like the angels and the possessors of knowledge, bear witness by assenting to the truth of that to which He bears witness concerning Himself. The creatures cannot reach the core of His majesty and tremendousness, and their bearing witness is nothing but assenting to the truth of the Real's bearing witness. Jaʿfar ibn MuḤammad said, "The bearing witness of people is built on four pillars: first fol lowing the commands, second avoiding prohibitions, third contentment, and fourth approval. " It is said that people's bearing witness is of three sorts: the bearing witness of the common people, the bearing witness of the elect, and the bearing witness of the elect of the elect.

**There is only One God, and no partners.**

Then, the Holy Prophet is asked to tell them: that is, He is one God, the only one worthy of worship who has no partners, sharers or associates in His pristine Divinity. (He is only One God) the true God is only One God. I am free from all that you associate as partners with Him. When he comes to know that it is really the Book of God, he should necessarily be satisfied with whatever is advocated therein. The missionary’s responsibility ends with his ‘preaching’, while that of the addressee ends only on his ‘fulfilling his religious obligations’. (O Allah, there is none Who can avert what You grant or give what You deprive, and no fortune ever helps the fortunate against You.) This is why Allah said,.

20.text:
Those to whom We gave the Scripture recognize him to be a true prophet as they recognize their own children. The verse turns from the idolaters to the people who had been given a book before, and it makes a claim about what they already know in their own hearts. Those to whom We gave the Scripture: the giving is named as a fact that puts them in a special position, since they hold the earlier writings and can read what was written there. recognize him to be a true prophet: the recognition is not described as a new discovery but as a thing they already have, and the sources explain that the earlier books carry a description of the one who was to come, with his city and his people and his qualities. as they recognize their own children: the likeness is chosen because a father does not need to be argued into recognizing his son, so the verse states that their knowledge is of the same kind, immediate and beyond doubt. Those who have ruined themselves will never believe: the second sentence names the ones among them who will not accept what they know, and the ruin is placed on them rather than on the evidence, since the evidence is settled. The verse before had ended with the Prophet told to refuse the testimony of the idolaters, and this verse brings in the people of the earlier book as the ones whose testimony would actually count. The verses that follow carry the same argument forward, so the reader is asked to notice that the refusal in the passage is not about proof but about what people will do with it.

**The people of the Book recognize him.**

Those to whom We have given the Scripture recognise him that is Muhammad by the descriptions of him in their Scripture as they recognise their sons; those of them who have forfeited their own souls do not believe in him. About that it was said: ‌ ‌ ; (That is, as for the Jews and Christians, they recognize Muhammad al-Mustafa as they would recognize their sons. The reason is that there is, in the Torah and Injil, a full description of the physical features of the Holy Prophet of his home city and then his post-emigration place of residence, and of his habits and morals and achievements - all this in such details that it leaves no room for doubt in the recognition of his identity. In the last verse , it was said that these people of the Book who, despite knowing the true identity of the Holy Prophet do not accept Islam were simply ruining themselves at their own hands: ‌ (Those, who have brought loss on themselves, they are not going to believe). That quality was : His forbearance will dominate his anger.' Then, he went to see the Holy Prophet made his test and found him a true bearer of this quality.

**The likeness of recognizing their own children.**

The Jews who were given the Torah and the Christians who were given the Gospel recognise the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ completely, just as they recognise their own children from other children. At this point, the simile given in the text is that of children - as they would recognize their sons.' Not said here is: as children recognize their parents.

**Those who have ruined themselves will not believe.**

They are the ones who have lost their own souls by making them enter the fire of Hell, and they will not believe. Those who have lost (destroyed) themselves will not believe And who does more wrong than he who invents a lie against Allah or rejects His Ayat? Ka'b Ibn al-Ashraf and his followers (will not believe) in Muhammad or the Qur'an.

**The edifice of false beliefs.**

But, on the Day of Judgement, when all the veils are torn asunder, and when he sees that all the supports except that of God were absolutely false, he will have no alternative but to contradict his own statements. In the Hereafter they will become the rejecters of those very things of which they had been proud of being attached to. The edifice of false beliefs and explanations they had constructed will be so totally destroyed that it will seem never to have existed.

21.text:
Who does more wrong than those who fabricate lies against Allah or deny His signs, Indeed — the verse is shaped as a question, and the question is not asked for news, since it is a way of naming the worst of deeds and of putting the answer beyond doubt. To fabricate a lie against Allah is the first of the two, and the sources give it a definite shape: a man invents the lie when he claims that Allah sent him while Allah did not send him, or when he attributes to Allah a partner who was never His. To deny His signs is the second, and the same words carry both, so the liar and the denier are put on one level: the one refuses the message and the other refuses the proof that carried it. Then the verse leaves the question and gives the sentence that answers it: the wrongdoers will never succeed. The name wrongdoers comes last, and it gathers both crimes under one word, since the fabricating and the denying are one injustice, and the failure is attached to the doers rather than to a particular act. The question was also a refutation of those who had been asking for proofs, since the verse turns the charge back on them and shows where the real loss lies, and the reader who has been taken through the earlier verses is now given the measure by which the two crimes are weighed.

**The lie invented against Allah.**

And who that is none does greater evil than he who invents a lie against God by ascribing to Him an associate or denies His signs? the Qur’ān; it is verily the case that they the evildoers shall not prosper on account of this. (Who doth greater wrong) and is more daring (than he who inventeth a lie against Allah) by associating with Him other gods (and denieth His revelations) Muhammad and the Qur'an? (And who does more wrong than he who invents a lie against Allah or rejects His Ayat?) meaning, there is no person more unjust than he who lies about Allah and claims that Allah has sent him, while Allah did not send him. The greatest wrongdoer is the person who attributes a partner to Allah and worships him together with Allah, or the person who denies Allah’s words that He revealed to His Messenger.

**The signs of Allah that were denied.**

There is no person more unjust than he who denies Allah's proofs, signs and evidences,. (Lo! the wrong-doers) the disbelievers and idolaters (will not be successful) will not escape or be safe from Allah's torment. Surely, both of these people will never acquire success, whoever falsely (claims that Allah sent him) and whoever refuses [Allah's Ayat]. Those who do wrong by ascribing partners to Allah and denying His verses will never succeed if they do not repent.

**The false edifice torn down.**

But, on the Day of Judgement, when all the veils are torn asunder, and when he sees that all the supports except that of God were absolutely false, he will have no alternative but to contradict his own statements. The edifice of false beliefs and explanations they had constructed will be so totally destroyed that it will seem never to have existed. In the Hereafter they will become the rejecters of those very things of which they had been proud of being attached to. In other words, such people at that time will become witnesses against their own falsity. Whenever a man makes entities other than God the centre of his attention, a magical halo gradually forms around them. If he has a false sense of satisfaction with the stand he has taken, it is because in this world of trial he is always successful in finding explanations and justifications in his support; he readily finds the words to reject arguments in favour of the Truth—so much so that he feels free to wilfully misinterpret truth and claim that the ‘real Truth’ is that which he has adopted.

Where are those gods you used to claim: the verse then gives the words of the question, and the claiming is what the question turns on, since the idols were partners in their claim and never in fact. The delay between the gathering and the questions is marked in the same verse, and the sources notice that the word then carries it, so the standing on that Day is long before the reckoning begins. The verses before had stated that the unjust and the deniers of truth will not receive salvation, and this verse shows what happens when they are gathered, so the reader is carried from the statement of the loss to the scene in which it unfolds. ‘Where are your partners that you used to claim were partners to Allah?’ "Where are your partners (false deities) whom you used to assert (as partners in worship with Allah)? (And on the Day We gather them together) all mankind on the Day of Judgement (We shall say unto those who ascribed partners (unto Allah): Where are those partners) idols (of your make-believe) that you worshipped and claimed they would intercede for you? But, by giving some thought to the general happenings and conditions of the Day of Resurrection, it could be said that Allah Ta ala had given them the freedom to say things as they used to say in their life of the mortal world so that everyone present on the Day of Resurrection could see their full profile and get to know that these people did not stop at disbelief and polytheism, but that they were also unmatched as liars, for they would not desist from lying at least on an occasion so horrifying. This is contrary to the test of the day of Resurrection where questions will be asked and answers given before Al-mighty Allah which means that no lie will work there even if resorted to. Another question which arises in this verse is about what has been said in some verses of the Qur'an - that Allah Almighty will not speak to the disbelievers and sinners - while, the present verse seems to be indicating clearly that such address will come to pass. About that, it has been said in Surah Yasin: ‌ 65 (That Day shall We set a seal on their mouths. But their hands will speak to Us, and their feet bear witness, to all that they did - 36:65). But, on the Day of Judgement, when all the veils are torn asunder, and when he sees that all the supports except that of God were absolutely false, he will have no alternative but to contradict his own statements. 24.text:
See how they will lie about themselves and how those gods they fabricated will fail them: the verse turns from what the idolaters will say to what the sight of them shows, and the address is to the Prophet, so the scene is held up for him to see and for the reader after him. The sources give the shape of that fabrication, since the worship had been given to beings that were not God but only a way to seek intercession and nearness, and the reader is shown what becomes of a hope built on that. The verb is also read as a forging and a coining, so the whole religion of the idolaters is presented as something fabricated, and the day of Resurrection is the place where the fabrication is exposed. In these two verses, it should be particularly borne in mind that the choice of free speech given to disbelievers on the day of Resurrection which they utilized by denying on false oath that they had any-thing to do with Shirk, is not without its implications. And on the night of the Mi raj (the Ascent to Heaven), the Holy Prophet saw a man having the corners of his mouth being slit apart which then fall back into their place and become as they were, and again they are slit apart ... something to keep happening to him throughout the day of Qiyamah. In verse 24, it was said: ‌ ‌ (See how they lied about themselves - and lost to them was all that they used to coin). But the which they invented will disappear from them And of them there are some who listen to you; but We have set veils on their hearts, so they understand it not, and deafness in their ears; if they see every one of the Ayat they will not believe therein; to the point that when they come to you to argue with you, those who disbelieve say: (and (by doing so) they destroy not but themselves, yet they perceive not.) This is the same old story which we have been hearing for such a long time.

**The reckoning that shapes a life.**

Out of these, the Belief in the 'Akhirah, the belief that there is a reckoning of deeds to come when good shall be rewarded and evil punished, has pragmatically the most revolutionary effects, as it channels every human deed into a particular direction. In the verses appearing here, special emphasis has been laid on the reckoning of the 'Akhirah, its rewards and punishments, and the true nature of the mortal world. These are principles which tell human beings who they are and what is the purpose of their life. This understanding brings a revolution in their lives by showing them the straight path. This is the reason why all subjects dealt with in the Qur'an revolve around these three. Tauhid (Oneness of Allah), Risalah (Prophethood) and 'Akhirah (Belief in the Hereafter). This type of life is thoroughly sinful, whether led in open denial of the Hereafter or without actually uttering the words of denial. On what basis does man rush towards worldly things—thinking them his own?
